children.content: Dialga is currently a very strong deck, largely due to its effective use of Mew. Dialga enables early energy ramp while also taking advantage of Mews Genome Hacking against decks like Palkia, without discarding any energy. Additionally, Cyrus is a powerful tool in both variants, as Dialga's Metallic Turbo attack applies early chip damage.
Melmetal is surprisingly viable due to Giant Cape, which significantly increases its effective HP. It can survive even 150-damage attacks, especially since Giovanni is currently not being played.

children.content: Exeggutor's primary partner is Venusaur, allowing it to leverage its Stage 1 status and deal damage with just one Grass Energy to apply early pressure.
Standard Variation: This version includes Venusaur, as Exeggutor is a durable Grass Pokémon capable of tanking hits.
Variation in Testing Another build explores the use of Victreebel to lure Basic Pokémon from the bench to the active position, enabling players to pick off the final points needed to secure victory.
Overall, Exeggutor's synergy with Venusaur provides a solid foundation, while innovative strategies are being tested to enhance its effectiveness in matches.

children.content: Garchomp is currently struggling in the meta due to many top decks having high HP and the ability to one-shot it. It can be fairly compared to its counterpart, Dragonite, which faces similar challenges.
There are two Garchomp decks that reached topped at tournaments
Mew – Uses Mew as a secondary attacker, but struggles against Dark decks like Darkrai.
Druddigon– Uses Druddigon to tank hits for Garchomp before going down, similar to how Dragonite functions, but still faces survivability issues. -BellaVGC

children.content: Infernape Giratina - the deck plays around with a lot of Pivots and benefiting of as a Cheap attacker. Making good use of Giratina switch into Infernape and then using Dawn.
Infernape Moltres excels at setting up both itself and Arcanine, but it lacks the high damage output that Charizard provides.

Dawn helps Moltres to become a attacker when you flip 1 head ,you can attack for 70 with Moltres on turn 2 to get a knock out against basic non-ex.
As a result, Infernape decklists either include or cut Arcanine, just like Charizard decks. It is still uncertain which of these two decks will prove to be the stronger option.

children.content: Pachirisu decks are split between 18t and Pikachu variants. Both decks are struggling against the current high damage meta.

This version utilizes early Sabrina to force the opponent into an switching and discarding the energy. Either switching out and losing momentum or accepting an early knockout. Additionally, when the opponent switches, Cyrus ensures that the second target is easily knocked out.

Pachirisu ⁠pikachu-ex
Pikachu decks come in many forms, and Pachirisu Pikachu has been the most surprising among them in tournament play due to Dawn.
The deck uses X-Speed to enable free retreats into Dawn. Dawn plays a crucial role by attaching 1 Energy from the Bench to the Active Pokémon. Since the deck relies on 2-Energy attackers, this setup effectively keeps Pikachu/Pachirisu at full health during switches, ensuring continuous pressure. -BellaVGC

All successful Palkia decks currently share one common theme: Manaphy Ramp. Starmie Variant – Palkia acts as a tank, allowing to tank for Staryu until it evolves into Starmie. The free retreat cost of Starmie then enables Palkia to switch back in and make use of the energy later again.

Pikachu has fallen from its former high-tier status. The deck previously relied on frequent retreats to mitigate prize loss and maintained a full bench of low-HP Pokémon. However, with the introduction of Cyrus, it now struggles to stay relevant. Despite this, Pikachu has gained some new tools, including Pachirisu, with the latest expansion.
-BellaVGC
